Bug_Details:
Comparing protobuf fields of type String using reference equality Comparing strings with == is almost always an error, but it is an error 100% of
the time when one of the strings is a protobuf field. Additionally, protobuf
fields cannot be null, so Object.equals(Object) is always more correct.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by comparing the string values of two protobuf messages using reference equality (==) instead of content equality (.equals()). This is incorrect because even if the strings have the same content, they are different objects in memory.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test cases trigger the bug by creating two ExampleMessage objects with the same string value but different references. The showBug method compares these string values using reference equality (==), which will incorrectly return true if the objects are the same and false if they are different, leading to test failures.
